**SunnyShade Hats (SSH)**

SunnyShade Hats is a private limited company (Ltd) that designs and makes sun hats. It started six years ago and now has 40 production workers and 8 office staff in City M. SSH sells hats on its website and to independent clothes shops. The owners, Naila and Amir, want to expand by launching a new eco-friendly range called OceanWave.

SSH currently buys most fabric from Country T and pays in US dollars (USD). Fabric prices have been stable, but transport costs are rising. The company uses industrial sewing machines. A bank loan of £300 000 was used last year to buy new machines.

Quality is very important. Recent checks show defect rates have increased as new staff have joined. SSH plans to hire 20 more machinists. Managers are deciding how to motivate staff to increase output and reduce defects. Two ideas are:

- Piece rate (a payment per hat made)
- Job rotation with extra skills training

SSH is also reviewing its packaging for online orders. The current plastic mailer is cheap and waterproof. A supplier has offered recyclable cardboard packaging that looks premium but costs more and may be less water-resistant.

To support decision making, the finance manager prepared weekly cost data and a summary of assets and liabilities for this year and last year. The marketing team has created a simple online advert for the OceanWave launch. A news article has also highlighted changes in the economy that could affect SSH.

### Appendix 1 – Online advert (draft)

**SUNNYSHADE – OCEANWAVE**
Light • durable • **made from recycled fibres**
Intro price: **£24.99**
Free head-size guide • Free returns
Follow us @SunnyShadeHats

### Appendix 2 – Statement of financial position items (end of year)

| **Item** | **2025 (£)** | **2026 (£)** |
|---|---|---|
| Inventories | 120,000 | 90,000 |
| Trade receivables | 180,000 | 210,000 |
| Cash | 40,000 | 10,000 |
| Trade payables | 160,000 | 190,000 |
| Bank overdraft | 0 | 50,000 |
| Bank loan (long term) | 300,000 | 300,000 |

### Appendix 3 – Business news (extract)

The economy is facing mixed news this month. The local currency has dropped 8% against the US dollar since January, making imports more expensive. At the same time, the government announced a 5% rise in the minimum wage to help workers cope with higher living costs. Meanwhile, the central bank cut interest rates by one percentage point in a bid to boost economic growth and encourage more borrowing and investment.

### Appendix 4 – Weekly cost and output (current line)

| **Measure** | **Value** |
|---|---|
| Output (hats per week) | 3,000 |
| Fixed costs per week | £6,000 |
| Total variable costs per week | £15,000 |

Explain four benefits of written employment contracts for machinists.

Refer to the following [insert](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2025/09/37160_Paper%202%20Set%20A%20Insert.pdf) when answering the question.
parts.solution_md:
Written contracts set out duties and standards clearly **[K]**, so machinists understand quality procedures and reduce the current defect trend that management has identified** [Ap]**

Contracts support fair, legal pay including minimum-wage compliance **[K]**, which reduces risk when the minimum wage rises by 5% next month and ensures payroll accuracy** [Ap]**

Having agreed hours and overtime rules improves planning **[K]**, allowing SSH to schedule staffing to hit the 3 000 units per week output while training happens ** [Ap]**

Contracts reduce misunderstandings and grievances **[K]**, so time is not lost to disputes and managers can focus on OceanWave production targets** [Ap]**

Cell Covers (CC)

Aisha worked for several years for a company that repairs mobile (cell) phones in country Z. She had always wanted to be her own boss and decided to leave her job to set up CC to produce covers for mobile phones. She went into partnership with her brother, Aruna. He worked as an Operations Manager for a company producing children’s clothes.

The sources of finance for the business were \$10 000 of savings from each partner and a bank loan of \$10 000. CC was also given a government grant to help the new business get started. CC leased a factory, bought some equipment and had to pay some expenses before the business had regular cash inflows.

CC’s current product is a range of standardised phone covers which are sold in the mass market. These are sold using a competitive pricing method through mobile phone shops. CC employs 10 skilled production workers who are paid just above the legal minimum wage. These workers have been trained how to operate the equipment and work as a team on the production line. During the production process there is a lot of waste plastic produced and CC sends this to landfill sites. The business has just completed its second year of trading.

CC is about to launch a new range of individual personalised phone covers. It will need to recruit 2 additional production workers. Aruna knows that the marketing mix for this new product may have to be different to the marketing mix used for the standardised products. The new product will be aimed at a niche market of high income consumers between the ages of 18 to 25. There are few other competitors in this market at present.

**Appendix 1 **

**Newspaper article in Main News**

Country Z has been in a recession but the economy is now  growing rapidly and unemployment is falling. With higher incomes the majority of people now own a mobile phone. This makes communication easier. Mobile banking is becoming more popular and it is used by a large percentage of the population.

**Appendix 2 **

**Advertisement for CC’s standardised mobile phone covers**

Do you want to protect your phone from damage? Then buy a phone cover from CC. Your phone will never be damaged if you use one of our high quality covers!!

We offer a range of standardised covers at competitive prices. The CC range has many different colours and designs so you will stand out from the crowd.

**Appendix 3 **

**Summary of CC’s financial information from the end of the second year of trading (\$)**

| Revenue | 800 000 |
|---|---|
| Cost of sales | 400 000 |
| Gross profit | 400 000 |
| Expenses | 250 000 |
| Profit | 150 000 |
| Current Assets | 20 000 |
| of which: Inventory | 5 000 |
| Current liabilities | 15 000 |

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of the following **three **methods of employee selection. Which method should CC use when recruiting production workers? **Justify **your answer.

- Application form
- Interview
- Aptitude tests

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2020-paper-22-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
Application forms provide detailed information for comparing candidates' qualifications to operate CC's new production equipment **[Ap]**. However, reviewing forms is time-consuming, and applicants may not be entirely truthful about their skills, which may lead to CC appointing the wrong applicant **[An]**

Interviews allow Aisha to assess applicants' personalities face-to-face. This is crucial, as CC needs team players to work alongside the existing ten production line workers **[Ap]**. Interviews also let applicants ask questions, ensuring they understand the job requirements before they accept the job **[An]**. However, they do not allow candidates to demonstrate practical production line skills **[An]**

Aptitude tests show if applicants can perform the job effectively, which is important for operating CC's machinery efficiently **[An]** . They can show how well candidates interact with the other skilled workers **[Ap]**. However, they may not reveal an applicant's ability to learn skills for CC's new production process **[Ap] **which is likely to be somewhat different to allow for personalisation** [Ap]**

CC should use interviews as the primary selection method **[E]**. This will allow them to assess teamwork skills and explain the requirements for producing both standardised and new personalised phone covers **[Ap]**. As the involve face-to-face interaction, Aisha may find interviews an effective way to identify workers who will fit into CC's factory environment, collaborate well with current employees, and contribute to efficient production **[E]** as the business grows **[Ap]**. This is not possible with a written application form **[An]**. As aptitude tests may not reveal an applicant's ability to learn new skills for the different production processes CC intends to introduce, they will not give Aisha all of the information she needs to make the best choice  **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Application form**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Wide range of written information on each applicant **→** quicker first screen than interviewing everyone
>     - Forms can be laid side-by-side **→** makes it easier to compare candidates fairly
>     - Lists qualifications needed to run the machines **→** CC can see straight away who is trainable
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Takes time to read every form **→** slows the hiring process
>     - Applicants can exaggerate or lie **→** risk of short-listing the wrong people
> - **Interview**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Face-to-face meeting shows personality **→** judge whether the candidate will fit into a production-line team
>     - Lets managers test teamwork and communication skills **→** higher future motivation
>     - Applicants can ask questions **→** lowers the chance they quit soon after hiring
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - More time-consuming and costly than reading forms
>     - Confident talkers may impress even if their skills are weak **→** possibility of a poor hire
> - **Aptitude test**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Measures practical ability to operate equipment **→** candidates cannot fake skill
>     - Helps pick the most skilful worker **→** higher productivity and lower unit costs
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Tests can be expensive and time-consuming to design and run
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Application forms: a cheap, written record for easy comparison, but the information can be false and takes time to read
>   - Interviews: reveal personality and team fit, yet they are slower and may favour confident speakers over truly skilled workers
>   - Aptitude tests: hard proof of machine-handling skills, but they add cost and extend the recruitment timeline
>   - A balanced approach could be: application forms for short-listing → brief interviews for team fit → a short aptitude test before the final offer to combine speed, fairness and reliability

**Safari Adventures (SA) **

Tokumbo is a sole trader. He started SA 2 years ago in country X. Tokumbo had previously worked for a company selling holidays. SA organises safari tours which take tourists to view wild animals on a game reserve. Most of SA’s customers are tourists from other countries. Tokumbo did not have any objectives when he started SA but knows they are important for his business.

SA uses its own vehicles for the 7 day safari tours and provides accommodation in small local hotels. Tokumbo employs 4 safari guides, 1 for each of the 4 vehicles. The safari guides drive the tourists around the game reserve. There is 1 additional employee who helps Tokumbo in the office with administration. Tokumbo thinks SA needs a website so tourists can book directly with them rather than booking through holiday companies that charge SA a fee.

Tokumbo is considering the following three options for the future growth of SA safari tours:

- Option 1 - increasing the number of safari guides and vehicles to increase the number of customers from the existing target market
- Option 2 – targeting young people who want to camp and sleep in a tent on their safari
- Option 3 - targeting high-income tourists who prefer to stay in luxury hotels

Information about these three options is outlined in Appendix 3.

Tokumbo plans to provide more training for his employees whichever option he chooses. He wants his existing employees to have a wider knowledge of the wild animals on the game reserve and to be able to provide high-quality customer service. Tokumbo has to decide which method of training to use.

**Appendix 1 **

**Newspaper article in Main News, September 2022 **

**Tourism takes off**

Country X is becoming a popular holiday destination for tourists from other countries.

There is an increased demand from high-income tourists who want to stay in luxury hotels whilst on safari tours. These tourists are willing to pay high prices. There is also a new trend for younger people who want cheaper holidays. They prefer to camp and sleep in tents on game reserves rather than stay in hotels.

Are the many safari businesses in country X ready to target these new markets?

The use of e-commerce to find and book safari tours by tourists from other countries is offering both opportunities and threats to businesses in country X.

The inflation rate in country X has increased to 4% which may affect some of our local safari businesses.

**Appendix 2 **

**Email from Tokumbo’s accountant**

To: Tokumbo

From: Accountant

Subject: Source of finance for the new vehicles

New vehicles will be needed whichever option you choose for the future growth of your business.

I have considered several sources of finance you could use for the new vehicles. Interest rates on bank loans have fallen to 2% whilst interest rates on savings are 3%. I think you should choose from one of the following sources:

- Leasing
- Bank loan
- Retained profit

We can meet to discuss these sources if that would help you to decide.

**Appendix 3 **

**SA’s three options for a 7 day safari tour**

|   | Option 1 More existing safari tours | Option 2 Camping safari tours | Option 3 Luxury safari tours |
|---|---|---|---|
| Forecast number of tourists per week | 16 | 32 | 10 |
| Total costs per week for SA to provide these safari tours | \$12 000 | \$8000 | \$20 000 |
| Average cost per tourist | \$750 | ? | ? |
| Price per tourist | \$1000 | \$400 | \$2400 |

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of two methods of training Tokumbo could use for his existing employees. Which method should he use? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2022-paper-21-case-study---new.pdf)[ ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2021-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
On-the-job training is specific to SA's safari tours, so employees learn exactly what they need to know about the animals **[Ap] **and customer service **[An]**. It's usually cheaper than off-the-job training because existing staff can provide the training. Also, safari tours **[Ap] **could include trainees as they learn while working, so SA would not miss out on revenue. However, the trainer might pass on bad habits, which could lead to safety concerns for tourists **[An]**

Off-the-job training involves experts providing training, so employees learn up-to-date information about game reserve species **[Ap]**. This could give SA an edge over competitors, as tour guides would be well informed, able to answer questions about habitats and conservation **[An]**. Training in the evening, could avoid losing tours during the day. However, while training, employees are paid but not working, which increases business costs **[An]**

Tokumbo should use on-the-job training because SA's employees will develop skills specific to SA's safari tours **[E]**. Off-the-job training might be more expensive and less focused on SA's needs **[E]**. On-the-job training will help Tokumbo's employees provide better service to tourists, which is crucial for the success of his safari business **[E]**, especially as it is facing increasing competition** [Ap]**

>

>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **On-the-job training**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Individual coaching on real tours **→** skills match SA’s safaris exactly
>     - Trainee still helps with the tour **→** some work is done while learning **→** less time wasted
>     - Uses existing staff as trainers **→** usually cheaper than paying for outside courses
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Trainer stops normal work to teach **→** short-term loss of output
>     - Trainer might pass on bad habits **→** poorer service and lower productivity
> - **Off-the-job training**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Lessons from animal experts **→** deeper knowledge and better guiding techniques
>     - Evening classes possible **→** no tours cancelled during the day
>     - Staff learn new skills current guides may not know **→** long-term productivity rises
>   - **Disadvantages**
>

>     - Guides are paid while learning but not touring **→** no income from safaris during training time

> 
> **Conclusion**
> 
> - On-the-job training is specific to safari tours and costs less, but skills may be limited to what current guides know and training can slow tours
> - Off-the-job training gives expert, up-to-date knowledge that could lift service quality and sales, yet it is more expensive and takes staff off tours temporarily

CC has manufactured chocolate bars in country X for 50 years. It imports most of its raw materials, such as cocoa beans. Over the last 10 years CC has expanded and now sells in other countries. Many of these countries have no trade restrictions. The Directors of CC know that globalisation has opportunities and threats for CC. CC produces a number of brands of chocolate bars, such as Tiabar, in country X. Its most popular chocolate bar, Choco, has the highest market share. parts.problem_md: Do you think experience is the most important factor for a business to consider when recruiting a new manager? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Experience is an important factor when recruiting a new manager, but it may not be the most important. An experienced person is likely to make fewer mistakes **[K]**, allowing the business to provide better service and increase brand loyalty. Experience shows they have the ability to do the job, potentially lowering training costs and time **[An]**

Other factors to consider include qualifications, which show technical ability, and personality **[K]**, as managers must be able to lead and work with subordinates in order for the business's objectives to be met **[An]**

Overall, experience is possibly the most important factor **[E]**, as it shows proven ability, allowing the new manager to add value quickly**. **While experience clearly demonstrates job capability, qualifications indicate knowledge and potential, which could be developed anyway with a candidate with experience **[E]**

parts.problem_md: Do you think off-the-job training is the best method of training for a service sector business to use? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Off-the-job training allows employees to learn without disrupting work while gaining new skills from experts outside of the business** [K]**. This can give them confidence and may increase their motivation, as the business they work for has invested money in their development. This may increase their loyalty and improve their ability to deliver good customer service **[An]**

On-the-job training could, though, be better for service businesses. Employees can keep working while learning **[K]** so productivity isn't lost, learning exactly how the business wants things done, as training is focused on skills needed for their specific role **[An]**

The best approach, in most cases, is to combine both on-the-job and off-the-job methods **[E]**. Some off-the-job training brings in new ideas, while on-the-job reinforces learning in the real work environment, delivering excellent customer service. A business should consider its specific needs, budget and the skills required when deciding on the most appropriate training methods to use **[E]**

> - Relevant requirements might include:
> 
>   - Experience - of selling jewellery
>   - Qualification/product knowledge - in retail management/gems
>   - Skills - e.g. Leadership skills – make sure new employees are well motived/communication skills – ensuring excellent customer service/ financial skills – make decision about which items of inventory to buy
>   - Trained – to operate the shop and supervise new employees
>   - Physical fitness – need to be on their feet all day in the shop
>   - Personal characteristics – friendly and welcoming to customers buying rings/easily approachable by customers when entering the new shop/able to speak the same language as local people in the area where the new shop is located
> - Application could include:
> 
>   - Operating the shop, making decisions about which items of inventory to buy, ensuring excellent customer service, ensuring new employees are motivated

parts.problem_md: **Identify two **legal controls over employment.
parts.solution_md:
Legal protection against unfair dismissal **[K]**

Legal protection against discrimination in the workplace** [K]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> A short sentence is usually enough to achieve the available marks in 'identify' questions

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Knowledge 2
> 
>   - Give a clearly-stated, valid definition to achieve both knowledge [K] marks
>   - 2 marks for a full definition, 1 mark for a partial definition
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - (Unfair) dismissal
>   - Discrimination/equal opportunities
>   - Health and safety
>   - Legal minimum wage
>   - Legal minimum age/child labour
>   - Contract of employment/conditions of employment
>   - Redundancy
> - Other appropriate responses should also be credited
> - Only award the first two responses given

parts.problem_md: **Define **‘job description’.
parts.solution_md:
A job description outlines the responsibilities and duties **[K] **to be carried out by someone employed to do a specific job **[K]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure your answer focuses on the job description rather than the person specification, which describes the characteristics of a preferred candidate

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Knowledge 2
> 
>   - Give a clearly-stated, valid definition to achieve both knowledge [K] marks
>   - 2 marks for a full definition, 1 mark for a partial definition
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Outlines the responsibilities and duties to be carried out by someone employed to do a specific job [2]
> 
>   - OR, A list of the key points about a job, job title, key duties, responsibilities, and accountabilities [2]
>   - OR, A description of the tasks, role, and responsibilities of a particular position [2]
>   - OR, What the job entails/explains the job with a list of suitable content [2]
> - Partial definition, e.g. What they must do in a job/list of content [1]

parts.problem_md: **Identify two **reasons why a business might offer training to its employees.
parts.solution_md:
Training may be needed when a new process or new equipment is introduced **[K]**

Training could be used to improve employee skills **[K]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> A short sentence is usually enough to achieve the available marks in 'identify' questions

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Knowledge 2
> 
>   - Clearly state two reasons to achieve both knowledge [K] marks
>   - 1 mark for each valid reason
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - To introduce a new process/new equipment
>   - Improve efficiency/productivity
>   - Increase output
>   - Reduce mistakes/fewer errors/better quality goods or services
>   - Improve employee skills
>   - Increase knowledge
>   - Improve motivation
>   - Help reduce labour turnover
>   - Decrease the chance of accidents
>   - Familiarise new employees with business/other employees
> - Other appropriate responses should also be credited
> - Only award the first two responses given

parts.problem_md: **Define **‘on-the-job training’.
parts.solution_md:
On-the-job training occurs at the place of work **[K]**, watching or following an experienced employee **[K]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Don't confuse on-the-job training, which can happen at any time during employment, with induction training, which is specifically provided when an employee starts to work for a business

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Knowledge 2
> 
>   - Two marks for a full definition, 1 mark for a partial definition
>   - The first mark is for understanding it is inside the workplace
>   - The 2nd mark is [+1] for stating by whom or providing example of where
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Training at the place of work, watching or following an experienced employee [2]
> 
>   - OR, Training at the place of work–usually the person does the actual job while an experienced employee observes and guides him or her, making corrections as required [2]
>   - OR, Watching a more experienced worker doing the job [2]
> - Partial definition e.g. training while you are working [1]
> - Do not award answers which clearly relate to induction

parts.problem_md: **Define **‘off-the-job training’.
parts.solution_md:
Off-the-job training takes place** **away from the workplace **[K] **and is usually undertaken by specialist trainers **[K]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Examples may help to demonstrate knowledge in this answer, but you must ensure you recognise that this form of training takes place away from the workplace

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Knowledge 2
> 
>   - Two marks for a full definition, 1 mark for a partial definition
>   - The first mark is for understanding it is away from workplace
>   - The 2nd mark is [+1] for stating by whom or providing example of where e.g. in a training centre
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Training that takes place **away** **from the workplace** usually by a specialist trainer(s) [2]
> 
>   - OR, Training that takes place **away from the workplace**, for example at college, university or a specialist training providers premises [2]
>   - OR, Training that **takes place away from the place **of work using methods such as courses/conferences/online learning [2]
> - Partial definition, e.g. training away from the workplace [1]
> - Do not award examples on own, as this does not define the term

parts.problem_md: **Identify four **stages of the recruitment process.
parts.solution_md:
Identify a vacancy **[K]**

Produce a job description **[K]**

Draw up a person specification **[K]**

Advertise the vacancy **[K]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure that you know the difference between a job description, which describes a job role, and a person specification, which describes the characteristics of a preferred candidate

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Knowledge 4
> 
>   - Clearly identify four stages to achieve knowledge [K] marks
>   - 1 mark for each valid stage
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Award 1 mark per stage, ** **four from:
> 
>   - Job analysis / identify vacancy
>   - Job description
>   - Person/job specification
>   - Advertising (the vacancy)
>   - Application forms sent out/received
>   - Short listing/screening
>   - Interview/testing
>   - Selection / job offer / hire
> - Other appropriate responses should also be credited
> - Only award the first four responses given
> - Answer must be from the business viewpoint not the applicants e.g. CV or letter of application

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> Alex started APB as a sole trader business 4 years ago. APB provides printing services for local businesses, such as leaflets and brochures. Alex thinks having a good location is important to any business. All APB’s 6 employees receive on-the-job training. Alex has a democratic leadership style and uses job rotation to help keep employees motivated. To meet an increase in demand, Alex plans to buy an additional printing machine. This will cost \$1 800. Alex has to decide on an appropriate source of finance.

**Outline one** advantage and **one **disadvantage to APB of using on-the-job training.
parts.solution_md:
An advantage is that output is produced while employees are training** [K] **so they are still able to print some brochures** [Ap]**

However, the trainer may not have the necessary skills to teach other workers **[K]** how to use the new printing machine effectively** [Ap]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> You must ensure that your answer contains one advantage and one disadvantage to gain both knowledge marks

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Knowledge 2; Application 2
> 
>   - Give two valid benefits to achieve both knowledge [K] marks
>   - For each benefit, refer to the business case study to achieve both application [Ap] marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Advantage:
>   
>     - Some output produced while training [k] so able to still print some brochures [ap]
>     - Costs less than off-the-job [k] and cost might be important issue as he is a sole trader [ap]
>     - Specific to business / control what is taught [k] using the printing machines [ap]
>   - Disadvantage:
>   
>     - Trainer may not produce as much output / potential disruption [k] when teaching the 6 employees [ap]
>     - Trainer may not have the necessary skills / may not know up-to- date methods [k] for the new machine [ap]
>     - Trainer may pass on bad habits / may be a poor-quality trainer [k]
>     - Employees make more mistakes when learning which increases waste [k]
>   - Other appropriate responses should also be credited
> - Application
> 
>   - To use words from the stem as application, the reference must be appropriate (i.e. make sense) in relation to the point being made
>   - The following words are likely to be appropriate for this question:
>   
>     - Sole trader
>     - Printing services / leaflets / brochures
>     - Printing / new machine
>     - 6 employees
>   - Other appropriate examples in context can still be credited
